title: Which cards test the rule?
hook: E, K, 4, 7, and the rule "a vowel has an even number on its back". Which do you turn?

knows: what "if … then …" means in everyday speech
doesNotKnow: that a rule "if P then Q" can only be broken by a case with P true and Q false, so you test it by hunting for that case, not by finding cases that agree

misconception: To test "if vowel, then even" you turn the vowel and the even number (looking for confirmation).
objective: The learner can say that only E and 7 can break "if a card shows a vowel, its back is even", because a rule "if P then Q" fails only when P is true and Q is false, and that turning the 4 can only agree with it.

claims.text: A rule "if P then Q" fails only when P is true and Q is false (it says nothing when P is false).
claims.source: Truth table of the material conditional: P → Q is false exactly in the row P true, Q false (derivation).
claims.note: Truth table of the material conditional recomputed: P→Q is F only in the row P=T, Q=F (TT T, TF F, FT T, FF T). "Says nothing when P is false" is the informal reading of the vacuously true rows; not false.

claims.text: With a letter on one side and a number on the other, and possible backs 4 or 7 (letter cards) and A or K (number cards), only E (with 7 behind it) and 7 (with a vowel, A, behind it) could break "if a card shows a vowel, its back is even"; K and 4 cannot whatever their backs, and the stage tags each back "breaks" or "fine" accordingly. Recall: for "if fragile, then a red sticker", only the fragile parcel and the green-sticker parcel can break it.
claims.source: company/domains/briefs/checks/math-wave-j-check.mjs label D1 (backs that break: E: [7]; K: []; 4: []; 7: [A]). Stage: breaks(front, back) = vowel on the letter side and odd number on the number side, in Demo.tsx. Recall is the same enumeration with P = fragile, Q = red sticker.
claims.note: Enumerated over the stage backs (4/7, A/K) and over every digit 0–9 and letter A–Z: E breaks with any odd digit, 7 breaks with any vowel, K and 4 never break. Stage tags in the walkthrough match (E:7 breaks, 7:A breaks, all others fine). Recall: P=fragile, Q=red; only fragile and green-sticker (not red) parcels can break it, assuming one sticker per parcel as the question implies.

recall.question: Rule: if a parcel is marked fragile, it has a red sticker. Four parcels show: fragile, not fragile, red sticker, green sticker. Which must you check?
recall.why: The rule fails only for a fragile parcel without a red sticker, so check the fragile one and the green-sticker one; the red-sticker parcel can only agree.
